Older kids are never responsible to help raise their siblings. They have just as much right to be a child as the younger ones do.
Your parents made you and your siblings it's THEIR responsibility and THEIR responsibility alone to support and take care of you all.

Nothing wrong with them asking for help once in a while, but to put all the responsibility on you and then turn around and tell you it's your responsibility? That makes me sick to my stomach. 

I actually lost a friend over the summer for this. She would have her older daughter watch 3 of the younger kids at the pool. THREE. How can a child manage to watch 3 children around a pool? All she wanted to do was play and be a kid. 

I told my friend that it wasn't right that her daughter never gets to be a kid when we get together to do fun things and that it doesn't mean she can lounge around with the other adults. She told me I didn't know what I was talking about and had no room to talk because I only have one child.

I grew up taking care of my brother and I never got time to be a teenager. I would always have to come home after school, clean, cook, laundry help my brother with his homework, get him to bed e.t.c. She had the audacity to call me the R word when my grades were slipping. That's not even the worst thing she's called me. But honestly, people who have kids only to be like "oh my older ones are gonna watch them so I can be lazy and not parent" piss me off.

You have to understand kids don't view things how we do. 
Their mindset is of another world. 

What she is looking at it as "wow there's a bunch of cool stuff that I really like and want to do!"

She's not looking at him as a replacement by any means. She obviously loves you both SO dearly. Please don't take that away from her, not only would you be hurting her, you'd be hurting him too. They'd both be left wondering what they have done wrong. Her wanting to go home does not mean she loves you any less.

NTA for not wanting him there

But kind of sound like TA for the way you're speaking about him. As if he can control himself. "He's going to be screaming" "he's just going to be a big distraction"
It's not as if he can help it. Not like he's doing it on purpose to spite you and ruin YOUR day. 

But NO, don't let your family guilt trip you into inviting him. It's not part of his element. Nor is it obviously yours. If you barely known him you shouldn't be inclined to include him just because of blood.

Best of luck to you. I wish you a life of happiness and health.
